problems.title: Reported weighted diversity exceeds its unweighted upper bound
problems.source_location: Eqs.(19),(21)â€“(22), PDF pp.23â€“24; Table 3, PDF p.8; Table C.3, PDF p.26
claim: Connectivity fractions \(c_i\in[0,1]\) and nonnegative distances define \(Q=N^{-2}\sum d_{ij}g_ig_j\), \(W=N^{-2}\sum d_{ij}g_ig_jc_ic_j\).
analysis: Termwise multiplication by \(c_ic_j\in[0,1]\) proves \(0\le W\le Q\); when the quality gates require \(c_i>1/2\), also \(W\ge Q/4\). Yet common-scale printed pairs include B-Global Chair \((0.15,1.25)\), B-Global Table \((0.20,1.40)\), B-Global with symmetry Chair \((0.43,1.21)\), and DGL with symmetry Chair \((1.66,1.73)\). Even favorable two-decimal rounding leaves respective upper-bound excesses \(1.09,1.19,0.77,0.06\). Five printed occurrences represent four distinct entries. The first two baseline pairs already occur in the earlier 3DHPA paper; CFPAâ€™s own main pairs satisfy the bounds.
result: These entries cannot simultaneously follow the stated paired definitions and units. Which value or protocol is wrong cannot be determined from the inequality, and earlier occurrence is not a first-discovery claim.
repair: Recover paired contact accuracies/distances and actual aggregation units, recompute both metrics together, and replace only values established by those records. No replacement values are invented.

problems.title: One correct pair can erase the group symmetry loss
claim: The paper uses \(\sum_i\min_{j\in\Omega(i)}C_{ij}\); the source instead keeps \(\min_{i,j\in G}C_{ij}\) for each interchangeable group.
analysis: Two identical centered parts use identity rotations, ground-truth translations \((-1/4,0,0),(1/4,0,0)\), and predictions \((-1/4,0,0),(0,0,0)\). Identity symmetry gives pair-cost matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1/2\\1/4&1/4\end{pmatrix}\). Any admissible sign flip leaves the second translation norm at least \(1/4\). The paperâ€™s summed minima give \(1/4\), but the group-wide minimum is \(0\). A mean/sum convention cannot convert zero into a positive penalty. The untouched release also lacks a required translation-weight argument; historical numerical tests used a disclosed uniform-weight adapter, not successful untouched training.
result: The reduction differs algebraically even under positive translation surrogates. Its published-run occurrence and accuracy effect remain unresolved.
repair: Minimize separately over allowed partners/variants for every predicted part, then apply the declared part/group normalization. This restores the reduction without certifying a full trained-model repair.
